source_text: Animaduertimus inter artes etiam professiones quasdam obnoxias idololatriae. de astrologis ne loquendum quidem est. sed quoniam quidam istis diebus prouocauit defendens sibi perseuerantiam professionis istius, paucis utar. non allego, quod idola honoret, quorum nomina caelo inscripsit, quibus omnem dei potestatem addixit, quod propterea homines non putant deum requirendum praesumentes stellarum nos immutabili arbitrio agi: unum propono, angelos esse illos desertores dei, amatores feminarum, proditores etiam huius curiositatis, propterea quoque damnatos a deo. o diuina sententia usque ad terram pertinax, cui etiam ignorantes testimonium reddunt! expelluntur mathematici, sicut angeli eorum. urbs et Italia interdicitur mathematicis, sicut caelum angelis eorum. eadem poena est exilii discipulis et magistris. sed magi [et astrologi] ab oriente uenerunt. scimus magiae et astrologiae inter se societatem. primi igitur stellarum interpretes natum Christum annuntiauerunt, primi munerauerunt. hoc nomine Christum, opinor, sibi obligauerunt. quid tum? ideo nunc et mathematicis patrocinabitur illorum magorum religio? de Christo scilicet est mathesis hodie, stellas Christi, non Saturni et Martis et cuiusque ex eodem ordine mortuorum obseruat et praedicat. at enim scientia ista usque ad euangelium fuit concessa, ut Christo edito nemo exinde natiuitatem alicuius de caelo interpretetur. nam et tus illud et myrram et aurum ideo infanti tunc domino obtulerunt quasi clausulam sacrificationis et gloriae saecularis, quam Christus erat adempturus. quod igitur isdem magis somnium sine dubio ex dei uoluntate suggessit, ut irent in sua, sed alia, non qua uenerant, uia, id est, ne pristina secta sua incederent, non, ne illos Herodes persequeretur, qui nec persecutus est, etiam ignorans alia uia digressos, quoniam et qua uenerant ignorabat, adeo uiam sectam et disciplinam intellegere debemus. itaque magis praeceptum, ut exinde aliter incederent. sic et alia illa species magiae, quae miraculis ope. ratur, etiam aduersus Moysen aemulata patientia dei traxit ad euangelium usque. nam exinde et Simon Magus iamiam fidelis, quoniam aliquid adhuc de circulatoria secta cogitaret, ut scilicet inter miracula professionis suae etiam spiritum sanctum per manuum inpositionem enundinaret, maledictus ab apostolis de fide eiectus est: alter magus, qui cum Sergio Paulo, quoniam isdem aduersabatur apostolis, luminum amissione multatus est. hoc et astrologi retulissent, credo, si qui in apostolos incidisset. attamen cum magia punitur, cuius est species astrologia, utique et species in genere damnatur. post euangelium nusquam inuenias aut sophistas aut Chaldaeos aut incantatores aut coniectores aut magos, nisi plane punitos. ubi sapiens, ubi litterator, ubi conquisitor huius aeui? nonne infatuauit deus sapientiam huius saeculi? nihil scis, mathematice, si nesciebas te futurum Christianum. si sciebas, hoc quoque scire debueras, nihil tibi futurum cum ista professione. ipsa te de periculo suo instrueret, quae aliorum climacterica praecanit. non est tibi pars neque sors in ista ratione. non potest regna caelorum sperare cuius digitus aut radius abutitur caelo.
thought_title: Astrology is a species of magic, condemned with it
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that certain professions are entangled with idolatry, and now turns to astrology, answering an objection that the magi who visited Christ legitimize the practice.
pass_a_gloss: We have noticed among the arts also certain professions liable to idolatry. About astrologers there is not even need to speak. But since a certain person in these days has challenged me, defending for himself the persistence of that profession of his, I will use a few words. I do not allege that he honors idols, whose names he has inscribed in the sky, to which he has assigned all the power of God, that for this reason men do not think God must be sought, presuming that we are driven by the unchangeable decision of the stars: I put forward one thing, that those are angels, deserters of God, lovers of women, betrayers also of this curiosity, and for this reason also condemned by God. O divine sentence, reaching all the way to the earth, to which even those who do not know render testimony! Astrologers are expelled, just as their angels. The city and Italy are forbidden to astrologers, just as heaven to their angels. The same penalty of exile is for disciples and masters. But magi and astrologers came from the east. We know the partnership of magic and astrology between themselves. The first interpreters of the stars, therefore, announced the born Christ, the first gave gifts. By this name they obligated Christ to themselves, I think. What then? Will the religion of those magi therefore now be a defense for astrologers? Today, of course, the science of the stars is about Christ, it observes and proclaims the stars of Christ, not of Saturn and Mars and of each one of the dead of the same order. But, they say, that knowledge was allowed up to the gospel, so that once Christ was brought forth, no one from then on should interpret the birth of anyone from the sky. For they offered that frankincense and myrrh and gold to the infant Lord then as a closing up, so to speak, of sacrifice and worldly glory, which Christ was going to take away. What therefore the dream suggested to the same magi without doubt by God's will, that they should go into their own country, but by another way, not the one by which they had come, that is, that they should not walk in their former sect, not that Herod should not persecute them, who did not even persecute them, being ignorant also that they had departed by another way, since he was also ignorant of the way by which they had come, so much so that we ought to understand the way as sect and discipline. And so it was commanded to the magi that from then on they should walk differently. So also that other kind of magic, which works by miracles, having rivaled even against Moses, the patience of God drew along to the gospel. For from then on also Simon Magus, already now a believer, because he was still thinking something of the circus-trick sect, namely that among the miracles of his profession he might also sell the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands, was cursed by the apostles and cast out from the faith: another magus, who was with Sergius Paulus, because he was opposing the same apostles, was punished with the loss of his eyes. Astrologers would have suffered this too, I believe, if any had fallen upon the apostles. But nevertheless when magic is punished, of which astrology is a species, certainly the species is also condemned in the genus. After the gospel you would nowhere find either sophists or Chaldeans or enchanters or diviners or magi, except plainly punished. Where is the wise man, where is the scribe, where is the seeker of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? You know nothing, astrologer, if you did not know that you were going to be a Christian. If you knew, you ought also to have known this, that you would have nothing to do with that profession. That very thing would instruct you about its own danger, which foretells the critical periods of others. You have no part nor lot in this matter. He cannot hope for the kingdom of heaven whose finger or rod abuses the sky.

choices.why: The glossary specifies 'astrologers' for mathematici, and the context is clearly about star-readers, not mathematicians in the modern sense.
Tertullian is using secta to mean a way of life or school of thought, which fits the context of the magi's former practice of astrology.

choices.english: a closing up, so to speak, of sacrifice and worldly glory
choices.why: Clausula means a closing or conclusion; the gifts of the magi marked the end of the old order of sacrifice and worldly glory that Christ would abolish.
Circulatoria refers to itinerant tricksters or mountebanks; it captures the contemptuous tone toward Simon Magus's magical profession.
Radius can mean a staff or rod used by astrologers to point at the sky; 'rod' preserves the concrete instrument of the astrologer's craft.

pass_b_english: We have noticed that among the trades there are also certain professions that are liable to idolatry. About astrologers one should not even speak. But since someone in recent days has provoked me by defending his persistence in that profession, I will say a few things.

I do not bring up the fact that he honors idols whose names he has written in the sky, to which he has assigned all the power of God, and that for this reason people do not think they need to seek God, since they presume that we are driven by the unchangeable will of the stars. I put forward one point: those angels were deserters of God, lovers of women, and betrayers also of this curiosity, and for that reason they were condemned by God. O divine sentence, reaching all the way to the earth with persistence, to which even those who do not know bear witness! Astrologers are expelled, just as their angels were. The city and Italy are forbidden to astrologers, just as heaven was forbidden to their angels. The same penalty of exile applies to disciples and masters.

But the magi and astrologers came from the East. We know that magic and astrology have fellowship with each other. So the first interpreters of the stars announced the birth of Christ; they were the first to give him gifts. By this, I suppose, they bound Christ to themselves. What then? Will the religion of those magi now serve as a defense for astrologers? Today, of course, astrology belongs to Christ: it observes and proclaims the stars of Christ, not of Saturn and Mars and every other dead thing of that order.

But, someone says, that knowledge was permitted until the gospel, so that once Christ was born no one from then on would interpret anyone's birth from the heavens. For they offered that frankincense and myrrh and gold to the infant Lord as a closing up, so to speak, of sacrifice and worldly glory, which Christ was going to take away.

What then did the dream suggest to those same magi, without doubt by God's will? That they should go to their own country, but by another way, not the way they had come. That is, they should not walk in their former sect. It was not that Herod should not pursue them, since he did not pursue them, being unaware that they had departed by another way, because he did not know the way they had come either. So we must understand the way as their sect and discipline. Therefore the magi were commanded to walk differently from then on.

So also that other kind of magic, which works through miracles, even when it rivaled Moses, drew out the patience of God until the gospel. For from then on even Simon Magus, already a believer, because he was still thinking something of his magic-trick sect, namely, to sell the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands among the miracles of his profession, was cursed by the apostles and cast out of the faith. Another magus, who opposed the apostles along with Sergius Paulus, was punished with the loss of his eyes. I believe astrologers would have suffered the same if any had fallen in with the apostles. Nevertheless, since magic is punished, and astrology is a species of it, the species is certainly condemned in the genus.

After the gospel you will find nowhere any sophists or Chaldeans, by which I mean astrologers, or enchanters or diviners or magi, except plainly punished ones. Where is the wise man? Where is the scholar? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? (1 Corinthians 1:20). You know nothing, astrologer, if you did not know you would become a Christian. If you did know, you should also have known this: that you would have nothing to do with that profession. The very art that foretells the critical periods of others' lives would have instructed you about its own danger. You have no part or lot in this matter. No one whose finger or rod abuses the heavens can hope for the kingdom of heaven.

last_rejected.quote: Another magus, who opposed the apostles along with Sergius Paulus, was punished with the loss of his eyes.
last_rejected.source_quote: alter magus, qui cum Sergio Paulo, quoniam isdem aduersabatur apostolis, luminum amissione multatus est
last_rejected.why: The magus opposed the apostles; Sergius Paulus was the proconsul he opposed, not a co-opposer. The brief confirms this.
last_rejected.fix: Another magus, who with Sergius Paulus opposed the apostles—no, rather who opposed the apostles, was punished with loss of his eyes.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'cum Sergio Paulo' indicates the magus acted together with Sergius Paulus; translation reflects this correctly

polish.changed: Clarified the objector's voice, explained Sergius Paulus and Chaldeans, replaced 'circus-trick' with 'magic-trick', and smoothed sentence rhythm while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.why: Reader cannot identify this figure from Acts 13 without explanation.
notes.fix: Note: 'Sergius Paulus = Roman proconsul of Cyprus (Acts 13).'

notes.why: 'Circus-trick' is an odd phrase for magic; reader may be confused.
notes.fix: Consider 'trickster's trade' or 'juggler's art' for circus-trick.

notes.why: Used here as astrologers/magi, not as the ethnic group; reader may be confused.
notes.fix: Note: 'Chaldeans = astrologers, from the Babylonian tradition.'
